report.finding: There is no real drift. Running the model exactly as given (reset, simulate 0→40, 400 points, default cvode tolerances rel=1e-6/abs=1e-12) the total S1+S2+S3 stays at 10.0 to within floating-point roundoff (~1e-14) for the entire run, including at t=40. The 9.97 figure isn't reproducible from this model/solver combination — most likely it came from misreading the downsampled table (rounding several small numbers by eye and summing the rounded values, which can easily look like it's off by ~0.03) or from a different run/session state than the one described. Tightening tolerances further (rel=1e-10, abs=1e-14) gives the same result, confirming there's no meaningful integration error accumulating and no need for a smaller step size.
report.evidence: rr.reset(); res=rr.simulate(0,40,400,['time','S1','S2','S3']); tot=res[:,1]+res[:,2]+res[:,3] gives tot[0]=10.0, tot[-1]=10.000000000000004, min=9.99999999999999, max=10.000000000000004 — i.e. conserved to ~1e-15. Repeating with rel_tol=1e-10, abs_tol=1e-14 gives min=9.999999999999986, max=10.0, essentially identical. This rules out both accumulating integration error and any benefit from a smaller step size.

rr.reset()
res = rr.simulate(0,40,400, selections=['time','S1','S2','S3'])
tot = res[:,1]+res[:,2]+res[:,3]
print(tot[0], tot[-1], tot.min(), tot.max())

# double check with tighter tolerances just to be safe
rr.reset()
rr.integrator.setValue('relative_tolerance', 1e-10)
rr.integrator.setValue('absolute_tolerance', 1e-14)
res2 = rr.simulate(0,40,400, selections=['time','S1','S2','S3'])
tot2 = res2[:,1]+res2[:,2]+res2[:,3]
print(tot2.min(), tot2.max())
# restore
rr.reset()
rr.integrator.setValue('relative_tolerance', 1e-6)
rr.integrator.setValue('absolute_tolerance', 1e-12)
